# Extra tests to distinguish population variance (original) from sample variance (mutant)
# The mutant divides by (N-1) instead of N, causing a systematic difference in rstd.
# We use tighter tolerances and amplified weights to expose the discrepancy.

def check_tight(M, N, eps=1e-5, atol=1e-4):
    """Check with tighter absolute tolerance."""
    torch.manual_seed(0)
    x = -2.3 + 0.5 * torch.randn(M, N)
    w = torch.rand(N)
    b = torch.rand(N)
    ref = torch.nn.functional.layer_norm(x, (N,), w, b, eps)
    out = layer_norm(x, w, b, eps)
    assert torch.allclose(out, ref, atol=atol, rtol=0), f"tight mismatch {M}x{N}"

def check_amplified(M, N, eps=1e-5, weight_scale=1000.0, atol=1e-2):
    """Check with large constant weight to amplify the variance divisor difference."""
    torch.manual_seed(0)
    x = -2.3 + 0.5 * torch.randn(M, N)
    w = torch.full((N,), weight_scale)
    b = torch.zeros(N)
    ref = torch.nn.functional.layer_norm(x, (N,), w, b, eps)
    out = layer_norm(x, w, b, eps)
    assert torch.allclose(out, ref, atol=atol, rtol=0), f"amplified mismatch {M}x{N}"

# 1. Tight tolerance on single-block case (N=1024)
check_tight(4, 1024, atol=1e-4)

# 2. Tight tolerance on two-block case (N=2048)
check_tight(4, 2048, atol=1e-4)

# 3. Amplified weight on single row (M=1) to make the difference obvious even with loose tolerance
check_amplified(1, 1024, weight_scale=1000.0, atol=1e-2)
